title.zh: 卷四十 列傳第三十 魯爽 薛安都 鄧琬 宗越 吳喜 黃回
title.en: Volume 40 Biographies 30: Liu Shuang, Xue Andou, Deng Wan, Zong Yue, Wu Xi, Huang Hui
title.raw: 卷四十 列傳第三十 魯爽 薛安都 鄧琬 宗越 吳喜 黃回 Volume 40 Biographies 30: Liu Shuang, Xue Andou, Deng Wan, Zong Yue, Wu Xi, Huang Hui

sentences.zh: 爽少有武藝，魏太武知之，常置左右。

translations.literal: Shuang from youth had martial skill; the Wei Emperor Taiwu knew of it and often kept him at his side.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shuang was skilled in arms; Emperor Taiwu of Wei took note of him and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 及軌死，爽代為荊州刺史、襄陽公，鎮長社。

translations.literal: When Gui died, Shuang succeeded him as Inspector of Jingzhou and Duke of Xiangyang, garrisoning Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: After Gui died, Shuang replaced him as Inspector of Jingzhou and Duke of Xiangyang, with his seat at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 粗中使酒，數有過失，太武怒將誅之。

translations.literal: He was coarse and given to drink; he repeatedly committed faults, and Taiwu in anger was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Rough in manner and prone to drunkenness, he committed fault after fault until Taiwu, enraged, was ready to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 爽懼，密懷歸南計。

translations.literal: Shuang was afraid and secretly conceived a plan to return south.
translations.idiomatic: In fear, Shuang secretly laid plans to defect to the south.

sentences.zh: 次弟秀小字天念，頗有意略。

translations.literal: His next younger brother Xiu, whose childhood name was Tiannian, had considerable resourcefulness.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiu, courtesy name Tiannian, was notably shrewd and capable.

sentences.zh: 仕魏以軍功為中書郎，封廣陵侯。

translations.literal: Serving Wei, he rose through military merit to Central Secretariat Gentleman and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei service he won promotion through battle honors to Central Secretariat Gentleman and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 或告太武鄴人欲反，復遣秀檢察，並燒石季龍殘餘宮殿。

translations.literal: Someone reported to Taiwu that the people of Ye intended rebellion; he again sent Xiu to investigate, and also to burn the remaining palaces of Shi Jilong.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached Taiwu that the people of Ye were plotting revolt, he again dispatched Xiu to investigate and to burn the ruined palaces left from Shi Jilong.

sentences.zh: 秀常乘驛往返，是時病還遲，為太武所詰。

translations.literal: Xiu often traveled by post relay; on this occasion he was ill and returned late, and Taiwu questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu regularly rode the courier relays back and forth; this time illness delayed his return, and Taiwu called him to account.

sentences.zh: 秀復恐懼。

translations.literal: Xiu was afraid again.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu grew afraid once more.

sentences.zh: 太武尋南攻，因從度河。

translations.literal: Taiwu soon marched south to attack, and Xiu followed him across the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu soon afterward marched south on campaign, Xiu went with him across the river.

sentences.zh: 先是廣平人程天祚為殿中將軍，有武力。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cheng Tianzuo of Guangping had been a Palace Guard general and possessed martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cheng Tianzuo of Guangping had served as a Palace Guard general and was known for his fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，助戍彭城，為魏軍所獲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he helped garrison Pengcheng and was captured by Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 27 he was helping defend Pengcheng when Wei forces captured him.

sentences.zh: 以善針術，深被太武賞愛，封南安公，常置左右。

translations.literal: Because he excelled at acupuncture, he was deeply favored by Taiwu, enfeoffed as Duke of Nan'an, and constantly kept at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in acupuncture, he won Taiwu's deep regard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Nan'an, and was kept constantly at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 恒勸秀南歸，秀納之。

translations.literal: He constantly urged Xiu to return south, and Xiu accepted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He kept urging Xiu to defect southward, and Xiu took his advice.

sentences.zh: 及太武北還，與爽俱來奔。

translations.literal: When Taiwu returned north, he came over to the Song together with Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu marched back north, he crossed over with Shuang to join the Song.

sentences.zh: 文帝悅，以爽為司州刺史，秀為滎陽、潁川二郡太守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was pleased and appointed Shuang Inspector of Sizhou and Xiu Administrator of the two commanderies of Xingyang and Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was delighted: he made Shuang Inspector of Sizhou and Xiu Administrator of both Xingyang and Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 是歲元嘉二十八年也。

translations.literal: That year was the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: It was Yuanjia year 28.

sentences.zh: 魏毀其墳墓。

translations.literal: Wei destroyed their ancestral tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei razed their family graves.

sentences.zh: 明年四月入朝，時太武已崩，上更謀經略。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year they entered court; by then Taiwu had died, and the emperor renewed plans for northern campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: They came to court in the fourth month of the next year. Taiwu was already dead, and the throne turned again to plans for recovering the north.

sentences.zh: 五月，遣爽、秀及程天祚等出許、洛。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he sent Shuang, Xiu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others out toward Xu and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he dispatched Shuang, Xiu, Cheng Tianzuo, and others toward Xu and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨攻碻磝不拔，敗退，爽亦收眾南還。

translations.literal: Wang Xuemo attacked Qiaoyao but could not take it and retreated in defeat; Shuang also gathered his forces and returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo assaulted Qiaoyao without success and withdrew defeated; Shuang likewise gathered his troops and marched south.

sentences.zh: 三十年，元凶弑逆，南譙王義宣起兵入討，爽與雍州刺史臧質俱詣江陵。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year the crown prince committed regicide; the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan raised troops to punish him, and Shuang went with the Inspector of Yongzhou Zang Zhi to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In year 30 the crown prince murdered his father; the Prince of Nanqiao Yixuan took the field to punish the crime, and Shuang went with Zang Zhi, Inspector of Yongzhou, to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 事平，以爽為豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Shuang was made Inspector of Yuzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, Shuang was appointed Inspector of Yuzhou with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 至壽陽，便曲意賓客，爵命士人，畜仗聚馬，如寇將至。

translations.literal: On reaching Shouyang he at once curried favor with guests, ennobling scholars and gathering weapons and horses as though an enemy were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Shouyang he began flattering visitors, handing out ranks to men of letters, and stockpiling arms and horses as if invasion were imminent.

sentences.zh: 元凶之為逆也，秀在建鄴。

translations.literal: When the crown prince carried out his treason, Xiu was at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: While the crown prince was committing his crime, Xiu was in Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 元凶謂秀曰：「我為卿誅徐湛之矣，方相委任。

translations.literal: The crown prince said to Xiu: "I have killed Xu Bozhi for your sake and am about to entrust you with great responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince told Xiu, "I have killed Xu Bozhi on your account and mean to place great trust in you."

sentences.zh: 」以秀為右將軍，使攻新亭，秀因此歸順。

translations.literal: He made Xiu General of the Right and ordered him to attack Xinting; Xiu thereupon went over to the loyal side.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Xiu General of the Right and sent him against Xinting, but Xiu used the assignment to declare for the loyal cause.

sentences.zh: 孝武即位，以為司州刺史，加都督，領汝南太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, Xiu was made Inspector of Sizhou with overall command and concurrent Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xiaowu acceded, Xiu became Inspector of Sizhou with overall command, holding concurrently the post of Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年二月，義宣與爽謀反，報秋當同舉。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xiaojian, Yixuan and Shuang plotted rebellion and notified Qiu Dang to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Xiaojian year 1, Yixuan and Shuang conspired to rebel and sent word that Qiu Dang should rise with them.

sentences.zh: 爽狂酒乖謬，即日便起兵。

translations.literal: Shuang, wild with drink and perverse in judgment, rose in arms that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, drunken and reckless, took up arms the same day.

sentences.zh: 使其眾戴黃標，稱建平元年，竊造法服。

translations.literal: He had his troops wear yellow badges, proclaimed the first year of Jianping, and secretly manufactured imperial regalia.
translations.idiomatic: His men wore yellow insignia; he declared the Jianping era and had court robes and regalia made in secret.

sentences.zh: 義宣、質聞爽已處分，便狼狽同反。

translations.literal: When Yixuan and Zhi heard that Shuang had already acted, they rose in haste together.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Shuang had already moved, Yixuan and Zhi scrambled to rebel as well.

sentences.zh: 爽於是送所造輿服詣江陵，板義宣及臧質等文曰：「丞相劉今補天子名義宣，車騎臧今補丞相名質，平西朱今補車騎名修之；

translations.literal: Shuang then sent the carriages and robes he had made to Jiangling, with commissions for Yixuan and Zang Zhi reading: "Chancellor Liu is now confirmed as Son of Heaven, name Yixuan; Charioteer Zang is now confirmed as Chancellor, name Zhi; Pingxi Zhu is now confirmed as Charioteer, name Xiuzhi;"
translations.idiomatic: Shuang forwarded the regalia he had made to Jiangling with written commissions: "Chancellor Liu is hereby confirmed Son of Heaven, personal name Yixuan; Charioteer Zang is confirmed Chancellor, name Zhi; General Who Pacifies the West Zhu is confirmed Charioteer, name Xiuzhi;"

sentences.zh: 皆板到奉行。

translations.literal: all commissions to be obeyed on arrival.
translations.idiomatic: each commission to take effect on delivery.

sentences.zh: 」義宣駭愕，爽所送法物並留竟陵縣不聽進。

translations.literal: Yixuan was appalled; the ritual objects Shuang sent were all detained at Jingling county and not allowed forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan was stunned. He held Shuang's regalia at Jingling and refused to let it pass.

sentences.zh: 使爽直出曆陽，自採石濟軍，與質水陸俱下。

translations.literal: He ordered Shuang to march straight on Liyang and cross the army from Caishi, while Zhi came down by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shuang directly toward Liyang to ferry troops from Caishi, while Zhi advanced by land and river together.

sentences.zh: 左軍將軍薛安都與爽相遇，刺殺之，傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: The General of the Left Army Xue Andou met Shuang, stabbed him to death, and sent his head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Left Army Xue Andou encountered Shuang, killed him with a thrust, and forwarded his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 進平壽陽，子弟並伏誅。

translations.literal: The army then pacified Shouyang; his sons and younger brothers were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: They next took Shouyang; Shuang's sons and brothers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 薛安都

translations.literal: Xue Andou
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou

sentences.zh: 薛安都，河東汾陰人也。

translations.literal: Xue Andou was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Andou came from Fenyin in Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 世為強族，族姓有三千家，父廣為宗豪。

translations.literal: His clan had for generations been a powerful lineage; the surname numbered three thousand households, and his father Guang was a leading magnate of the lineage.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his house had been a great clan—some three thousand households bearing the name—and his father Guang was its leading magnate.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝定關、河，以為上党太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song secured Guanzhong and the Yellow River region, he appointed Guang Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Song took the passes and the middle Yellow River, he made Guang Administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 安都少以勇聞，身長七尺八寸，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Andou from youth was famed for courage; he stood seven feet eight inches tall and was skilled with bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Andou won early fame for valor. He stood seven feet eight inches and was expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 仕魏以軍功為雍州、秦州都統。

translations.literal: Serving Wei, he rose through military merit to overall commander of Yongzhou and Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei service he won promotion through battle honors to overall commander of Yong and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年來奔，求北還，構扇河、陝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia he came over to the Song, asked to return north, and stirred up trouble in the He and Shaanxi regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 21 he defected to the Song, sought permission to go back north, and incited unrest along the Yellow River and in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 文帝許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen agreed.

sentences.zh: 孝武鎮襄陽，板為北弘農太守。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu held Xiangyang, he commissioned Andou Administrator of Northern Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiaowu was stationed at Xiangyang, he appointed Andou Administrator of Northern Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 魏軍漸強，安都乃歸襄陽。

translations.literal: As Wei forces grew stronger, Andou returned to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei armies pressed harder, Andou fell back to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隨王誕板安都為建武將軍，隨柳元景向關、陝，率步騎居前，所向克捷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Prince Dan of Sui commissioned Andou General Who Establishes Martial Might; he followed Liu Yuanjing toward the passes and Shaanxi, leading infantry and cavalry in the van, and wherever he went he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 Prince Dan of Sui appointed Andou General Who Establishes Martial Might. He marched with Liu Yuanjing toward the passes and Shaanxi, infantry and cavalry in the lead, winning every engagement.

sentences.zh: 後孝武伐逆，安都領馬軍，與柳元景俱發。

translations.literal: Later, when Xiaowu campaigned against the usurper, Andou commanded the horse troops and set out with Liu Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu later marched to suppress the usurper, Andou led the cavalry and departed with Liu Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 孝武踐阼，除右軍將軍，率所領騎為前鋒，直入殿庭。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu took the throne, he was made General of the Right Army, led his cavalry as vanguard, and entered the palace hall directly.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiaowu's accession he was appointed General of the Right Army, led his horsemen as the vanguard, and rode straight into the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 以功封南鄉縣男。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanxiang.

sentences.zh: 安都初征關、陝，至臼口，夢仰視天，見天門開，謂左右曰：「汝等見天門開不？

translations.literal: When Andou first campaigned in the passes and Shaanxi, at Jiukou he dreamed that looking up at heaven he saw the Heavenly Gate open, and said to those beside him: "Do you see the Heavenly Gate open?"
translations.idiomatic: On his first campaign in the passes and Shaanxi, at Jiukou he dreamed he looked up and saw the Gate of Heaven swing open. He asked his attendants, "Do you see the Gate of Heaven open?"

sentences.zh: 」至是歎曰：「夢天門開，乃中興之象邪？」

translations.literal: At this he sighed and said: "To dream the Heavenly Gate opens—is that not an omen of restoration?"
translations.idiomatic: Now he sighed and said, "To dream the Gate of Heaven opens—was that not a sign of dynastic renewal?"

sentences.zh: 從弟道生亦以軍功為大司馬參軍，犯罪，為秣陵令庾淑之所鞭。

translations.literal: His cousin Daosheng also won through military merit the post of Senior Clerk in the Grand Marshal's office; he committed an offense and was flogged by Yu Shuzhi, magistrate of Moling.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Daosheng had likewise won a Grand Marshal clerkship through battle honors but broke the law and was beaten by Yu Shuzhi, magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 安都大怒，即日乃乘馬從數十人，令左右執矟，欲往殺淑之。

translations.literal: Andou was furious; that very day he mounted horse with several dozen men, ordered his attendants to take spears, and was about to go kill Shuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Andou flew into a rage. That same day he mounted with several dozen followers, spears in hand, and set out to kill Shuzhi.

sentences.zh: 行至朱雀航，逢柳元景，遙問曰：「薛公何之？

translations.literal: Reaching the Zhuque ford he met Liu Yuanjing, who called from afar: "Where is Lord Xue bound?"
translations.idiomatic: At the Zhuque crossing he met Liu Yuanjing, who called from a distance, "Where are you bound, Lord Xue?"

sentences.zh: 」安都躍馬至車後，曰：「小子庾淑之鞭我從弟，今指往刺殺之。

translations.literal: Andou spurred his horse to the rear of the carriage and said: "That stripling Yu Shuzhi flogged my cousin; I am going now to stab him to death."
translations.idiomatic: Andou galloped to the rear of Yuanjing's carriage and said, "That whelp Yu Shuzhi beat my cousin—I am off to run him through."

sentences.zh: 」元景慮其不可，駐車紿之曰：「小子無宜適，卿往與手甚快。

translations.literal: Yuanjing feared he could not be stopped, halted his carriage, and deceived him, saying: "The boy deserved it; you will find the work most satisfying."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing, fearing disaster, stopped and coaxed him: "The lad had it coming—you will enjoy the business thoroughly."

sentences.zh: 」安都既回馬，元景復呼之令下馬入車，因讓之曰：「卿從弟服章言論與寒細不異，且人身犯罪，理應加罰。

translations.literal: Andou had already turned his horse when Yuanjing called him again to dismount and enter the carriage, and reproved him: "Your cousin's dress and speech are no different from the meanest commoner's, and when a man commits a crime he ought to be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Andou was turning back when Yuanjing summoned him into the carriage and rebuked him: "Your cousin dresses and speaks like any lowborn fellow, and when a man breaks the law punishment is only right."

sentences.zh: 卿為朝廷勳臣，云何放恣，輒於都邑殺人。

translations.literal: You are a meritorious servant of the court—how can you indulge yourself and kill a man in the capital on a whim?
translations.idiomatic: You are one of the court's great servants of merit—how can you indulge yourself and murder someone in the capital at will?

sentences.zh: 非惟科律所不容，主上亦無辭相宥。

translations.literal: Not only will the statutes not tolerate it; the sovereign will have no grounds to pardon you."
translations.idiomatic: The law will not bear it, and the emperor will have no excuse to spare you."

sentences.zh: 」因載俱歸，安都乃止。

translations.literal: He then carried him back together, and Andou stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He drove back with Andou, who abandoned his plan.

sentences.zh: 其年以憚直免官。

translations.literal: That year he was removed from office for his bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was dismissed from office for his outspoken manner.

sentences.zh: 時王玄謨拒南郡王義宣、臧質于梁山，安都復領騎為支軍。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Xuemo was holding off the Prince of Nan Commandery Yixuan and Zang Zhi at Liangshan; Andou again led cavalry as a detached force.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuemo was then blocking Yixuan and Zang Zhi at Liangshan; Andou again commanded cavalry as a separate wing.

sentences.zh: 義宣遣將劉諶之及臧質攻玄謨。

translations.literal: Yixuan sent the generals Liu Chenzhi and Zang Zhi to attack Xuemo.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan sent Liu Chenzhi and Zang Zhi against Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨命眾軍擊之，使安都引騎出賊陣右橫擊陷之，賊遂大潰。

translations.literal: Xuemo ordered the armies to strike; he had Andou lead cavalry out to the enemy's right flank in a lateral charge that broke them, and the rebels were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo ordered a general assault and sent Andou's horsemen to strike the enemy's right flank; the line collapsed and the rebels fled in rout.

sentences.zh: 轉太子右衛率。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 大明元年，魏軍向無鹽，遣安都領馬軍，東陽太守沈法系統水軍，並受徐州刺史申坦節度。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daming, Wei forces moved on Wuyan; Andou was sent to command the horse troops, the Administrator of Dongyang Shen Faxing to command the naval forces, both under the direction of the Inspector of Xuzhou Shen Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 1 Wei armies advanced on Wuyan. Andou led the cavalry, Shen Faxing of Dongyang the fleet, both under Inspector of Xuzhou Shen Tan.

sentences.zh: 時魏軍已去，坦求回軍討任榛見許。

translations.literal: The Wei army had already withdrawn; Tan requested permission to turn back and attack Ren Zhen, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei forces had already left. Tan asked leave to turn back and crush Ren Zhen, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 會天旱，水泉多竭，人馬疲困，不能遠追。

translations.literal: But drought came, springs ran low, men and horses were worn out, and they could not pursue far.
translations.idiomatic: Drought followed; water failed; men and horses were exhausted; they could not pursue.

sentences.zh: 安都、法系白衣領職，坦系尚方。

translations.literal: Andou and Faxing retained their posts in plain dress; Tan was imprisoned in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Andou and Faxing kept their titles but served in plain dress; Tan was sent to the Imperial Workshop in bonds.

sentences.zh: 任榛大抵在任城界，積世逋叛所聚，棘榛深密，難為用師，故能久自保藏，屢為人患。

translations.literal: Ren Zhen lay mostly within Rencheng; for generations fugitives and rebels had gathered there; thorn scrub was dense and troops hard to use, so they could long protect themselves and were repeatedly a menace.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhen lay chiefly in Rencheng, a haunt of rebels for generations. Dense thorn scrub made campaigning difficult, so the band could endure and plague the region again and again.

sentences.zh: 安都明年復職，改封武昌縣侯。

translations.literal: The next year Andou was restored to office and his fief changed to Marquis of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Andou returned to office and was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，為平北將軍、徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Xuzhou, with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe year 1 he became General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Xuzhou, with overall military authority.

sentences.zh: 時武衛將軍王廣之領軍隸劉勉，攻殷琰于壽陽，道固部將傅靈越為廣之軍人所禽，厲聲曰：「我傅靈越也。

translations.literal: At the time the Martial Guard General Wang Guangzhi led troops under Liu Mian to besiege Yin Yan at Shouyang; Fu Lingyue, a lieutenant of Dao Gu, was captured by Guangzhi's soldiers and cried out in a loud voice: "I am Fu Lingyue!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guangzhi of the Martial Guard was then campaigning under Liu Mian against Yin Yan at Shouyang. Fu Lingyue, an officer of Dao Gu, was seized by Guangzhi's men and shouted, "I am Fu Lingyue!"

sentences.zh: 汝得賊何不即殺。

translations.literal: You have taken a rebel—why do you not kill him at once?
translations.idiomatic: You have your enemy—why not kill him on the spot?

sentences.zh: 」時生送詣勉，勉躬自慰勞，詰其叛逆。

translations.literal: They sent him alive to Mian; Mian personally comforted him and questioned him about his rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: They delivered him alive to Mian, who received him kindly and asked why he had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「九州唱義，豈獨在我。

translations.literal: He answered: "The nine provinces have risen in righteous cause—how can the guilt be mine alone?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The whole realm has taken up righteous arms—why should I alone bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 」勉又問：「卿何不早歸天闕，乃逃命草間？

translations.literal: Mian asked again: "Why did you not earlier return to the imperial court, but fled for your life among the weeds?"
translations.idiomatic: Mian pressed him: "Why did you not come in to the throne earlier instead of skulking in the brush?"

sentences.zh: 」靈越曰：「薛公舉兵淮北，威震天下，不能專任智勇，委付子侄，致敗之由，實在於此。

translations.literal: Lingyue said: "When Lord Xue raised arms north of the Huai, his might shook the realm; he could not rely on his own wisdom and courage alone but entrusted command to sons and nephews—the true reason for defeat lies in that."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue said, "When Lord Xue raised the north Huai, his fame shook the world; yet he would not trust his own judgment and gave command to sons and nephews—that is why he was ruined."

sentences.zh: 人生歸於一死，實無面求活。

translations.literal: A man's life ends in death; I truly have no face left to beg for life."
translations.idiomatic: Life ends in death; I have no face left to beg for mercy."

sentences.zh: 」勉壯其意，送還建鄴。

translations.literal: Mian admired his spirit and sent him back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Mian respected his bearing and sent him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 明帝欲加原宥，靈越辭對如一，終不回改，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wished to pardon him, but Lingyue answered as before and would not change; he was therefore executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming meant to spare him, but Lingyue answered just as firmly and would not relent, so he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 靈越，清河人也。

translations.literal: Lingyue was a native of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 子勳平定，安都遣別駕從事史畢眾愛、下邳太守王煥等奏啟事詣明帝歸款。

translations.literal: After Zixun's rebellion was pacified, Andou sent his Registrar Bi Zhong'ai, the Administrator of Xiapi Wang Huan, and others with memorials to Emperor Ming offering submission.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zixun's revolt was crushed, Andou sent his registrar Bi Zhong'ai, Wang Huan of Xiapi, and others with memorials pledging loyalty to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 索兒之死也，安都使柳光世守下邳，至是亦率所領歸降。

translations.literal: When Suo'er died, Andou had posted Liu Guangshi to hold Xiapi; he too now led his command in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After Suo'er's death Andou had left Liu Guangshi holding Xiapi; he now brought his troops over as well.

sentences.zh: 帝以四方已平，欲示威於淮外，遣張永、沈攸之以重軍迎安都，懼不免罪，遂降魏。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking the realm already pacified, wished to display might beyond the Huai and sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a heavy force to receive Andou; fearing he could not escape punishment, he thereupon surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Believing the empire at peace, the emperor meant to awe the Huai frontier and sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi with a large army to take Andou into custody. Fearful of punishment, Andou defected to Wei.

sentences.zh: 深，安都從子也。

translations.literal: Shen was Andou's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was Andou's nephew.

sentences.zh: 本名道深，避齊高帝偏諱改焉。

translations.literal: His original name was Daoshen; it was changed to avoid the taboo of the Qi Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Born Daoshen, he changed his name to avoid the taboo of Qi's founding emperor.

sentences.zh: 安都以彭城降魏，親族皆入北。

translations.literal: When Andou surrendered Pengcheng to Wei, his kin all went north.
translations.idiomatic: When Andou yielded Pengcheng to Wei, his entire clan crossed north.

sentences.zh: 高帝鎮淮陰，深遁來，委身自結于高帝。

translations.literal: When the Qi emperor was stationed at Huaiyin, Shen fled to join him and devoted himself to winning the emperor's trust.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Qi emperor held Huaiyin, Shen slipped south to attach himself and earn his favor.

sentences.zh: 果乾有氣力。

translations.literal: He was resolute, capable, and full of strength.
translations.idiomatic: Bold, capable, and physically powerful.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽末，以軍功至驍騎將軍、軍主，封竟陵侯。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanyuan reign of Song he rose through military merit to General of Valiant Cavalry and army commander, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: By the close of Song's Yuanyuan era he had won his way to General of Valiant Cavalry and independent command, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬字元琰，豫章南昌人也。

translations.literal: Deng Wan, style name Yuanyan, was a native of Nanchang in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan, courtesy name Yuanyan, was from Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父胤之，宋孝武征虜長史、光祿勳。

translations.literal: His father Yinzhi was Chief of Staff to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians under Emperor Xiaowu of Song and Minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yinzhi had been Chief of Staff to Emperor Xiaowu's General Who Conquers the Barbarians and later Minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 孝武起義初，琬為南海太守，以弟瓊與臧質同逆遠徙，仍停廣州，久之得還。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaowu's uprising Wan was Administrator of Nanhai; because his brother Qiong joined Zang Zhi's rebellion he was exiled far away and remained at Guangzhou, only returning after a long interval.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu first raised the standard, Wan was Administrator of Nanhai. His brother Qiong had followed Zang Zhi in revolt and was banished far off, so Wan stayed at Guangzhou and did not return for many years.

sentences.zh: 歷位丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He held successive posts, including Assistant in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served in a series of posts, among them Assistant Magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 大明七年，車駕幸曆陽，追思在蕃之舊，擢琬為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming the emperor visited Liyang and, recalling old ties from his days as a prince, promoted Wan to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 7 the emperor visited Liyang, remembered their bond from his princely days, and promoted Wan to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為晉安王子勳鎮軍長史、尋陽內史，行江州事。

translations.literal: The following year he went out as Chief Clerk to the Prince of Jin'an Zixun's headquarters army and Interior Administrator of Xunyang, acting for the affairs of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left court as Chief Clerk on the staff of Prince Zixun of Jin'an and Interior Administrator of Xunyang, with acting authority over Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝以文帝、孝武並次居第三，以登極位。

translations.literal: The deposed emperor noted that both Emperor Wen and Emperor Xiaowu had been third in succession order when they took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor had noted that both Emperor Wen and Emperor Xiaowu reached the throne while third in line of succession.

sentences.zh: 子勳次第既同，深致嫌疑，因何邁之謀，乃遣使齎藥賜死。

translations.literal: Zixun was in the same order of succession, which aroused deep suspicion; on He Mai's counsel an envoy was sent bearing poison to grant him death.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun stood in the same succession rank, which bred deep suspicion; on He Mai's advice the court sent an envoy with poison to order his death.

sentences.zh: 使至，子勳典簽謝道遇、主帥潘欣之、侍書褚靈嗣等馳以告琬，泣涕請計。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, Zixun's registrar Xie Daoyu, commander Pan Xinzhi, attendant scribe Chu Lingsi, and others galloped to tell Wan, weeping and begging for a plan.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy arrived; Zixun's registrar Xie Daoyu, staff commander Pan Xinzhi, attendant scribe Chu Lingsi, and others raced to Wan in tears, pleading for counsel.

sentences.zh: 琬曰：「身南土寒士，蒙先帝殊恩，以愛子見托，當以死報效。

translations.literal: Wan said: "I am a humble scholar of the south, who received the late emperor's special grace when he entrusted his beloved son to me; I must repay that with my life."
translations.idiomatic: Wan said, "I am only a poor scholar of the south. The late emperor favored me and entrusted his beloved son to my care—I owe him my life in return."

sentences.zh: 」景和元年冬，子勳戎服出聽事宣旨，欲舉兵，四坐未答。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Jinghe, Zixun came out in armor to the audience hall to receive the decree and wished to raise troops; those seated all around did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in Jinghe year 1, Zixun appeared at court in armor to hear the decree and proposed to take up arms; no one in the hall spoke.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍陶亮曰：「請效死前驅。

translations.literal: Recorder Liu Tao Liang said: "I beg to die leading the vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: The recorder Tao Liang said, "Let me die in the van."

sentences.zh: 」眾並奉旨。

translations.literal: The assembly all accepted the order.
translations.idiomatic: All present pledged obedience.

sentences.zh: 會明帝定亂，進子勳號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming had settled the turmoil, Zixun was advanced to Charioteer and Grand Master with the privilege of an independent staff equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Ming was crushing the revolt, Zixun was promoted to Charioteer and Grand Master with staff equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 令書至，諸佐史並喜造琬曰：「暴亂既除，殿下又開黃合，實為公私大慶。

translations.literal: When the written order arrived, the staff all came joyfully to Wan and said: "The violent disorder is ended, and Your Highness has opened the Yellow Registry—this is great rejoicing for public and private alike."
translations.idiomatic: The order arrived and the staff flocked to Wan in delight: "The rebellion is over and Your Highness has opened the Yellow Registry—a blessing for us all."

sentences.zh: 」琬以子勳次第居三，又以尋陽起事，有符孝武，理必萬克。

translations.literal: Wan thought that Zixun, third in succession, had also risen from Xunyang, matching Xiaowu's case, and that victory was certain by reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wan reasoned that Zixun, like Xiaowu, was third in line and had raised arms from Xunyang—success was inevitable.

sentences.zh: 乃取令書投地曰：「殿下當開端門，黃合是吾徒事耳。

translations.literal: He then took the order and threw it to the ground, saying: "Your Highness should open the Vermilion Gate; the Yellow Registry is our concern alone."
translations.idiomatic: He flung the order down and said, "Your Highness must open the Vermilion Gate—the Yellow Registry is work for men like us."

sentences.zh: 」眾並駭愕。

translations.literal: The assembly was all appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was stunned.

sentences.zh: 琬與陶亮等繕甲器，徵兵四方。

translations.literal: Wan with Tao Liang and others repaired armor and weapons and raised troops from all quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wan and Tao Liang repaired arms and summoned soldiers from every direction.

sentences.zh: 郢州刺史安陸王子綏、荊州刺史臨海王子頊、會稽太守尋陽王子房、雍州刺史袁顗、梁州刺史柳元怙、益州刺史蕭惠開、廣州刺史袁曇遠、徐州刺史薛安都、青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固、湘州行事何慧文、吳郡太守顧琛、吳興太守王曇生、晉陵太守袁標、義興太守劉延熙並同叛逆。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yingzhou, Prince Zisui of Anlu; the Inspector of Jingzhou, Prince Zixu of Linhai; the Administrator of Kuaiji, Prince Zifang of Xunyang; the Inspector of Yongzhou Yuan Yan; the Inspector of Liangzhou Liu Yuanku; the Inspector of Yizhou Xiao Huikai; the Inspector of Guangzhou Yuan Tanyuan; the Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andou; the Inspector of Qingzhou Shen Wenxiu; the Inspector of Jizhou Cui Daogu; the acting head of Xiangzhou He Huiwen; the Administrator of Wu Commandery Gu Chen; the Administrator of Wuxing Wang Tansheng; the Administrator of Jinling Yuan Biao; and the Administrator of Yixing Liu Yanxi all rebelled together.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zisui of Anlu in Yingzhou, Prince Zixu of Linhai in Jingzhou, Prince Zifang of Xunyang in Kuaiji, Yuan Yan in Yongzhou, Liu Yuanku in Liangzhou, Xiao Huikai in Yizhou, Yuan Tanyuan in Guangzhou, Xue Andou in Xuzhou, Shen Wenxiu in Qingzhou, Cui Daogu in Jizhou, He Huiwen acting in Xiangzhou, Gu Chen in Wu, Wang Tansheng in Wuxing, Yuan Biao in Jinling, and Liu Yanxi in Yixing all rose together.

sentences.zh: 琬乃建牙于桑尾，傳檄建鄴，購明帝萬戶侯，布絹二萬匹，金銀五百斤，其餘各有差。

translations.literal: Wan then raised his standard at Sangwei, sent proclamations to Jiankang, and offered a reward of ten-thousand-household marquisate for Ming, twenty thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and five hundred jin of gold and silver, with other rewards graded below.
translations.idiomatic: Wan raised his banner at Sangwei, issued proclamations to Jiankang, and offered ten-thousand-household marquisate, twenty thousand bolts of silk, five hundred jin of gold and silver for Ming's head, with lesser prizes besides.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣荊州典簽邵宰乘驛還江陵，經過襄陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent the Jingzhou registrar Shao Zai by post relay back to Jiangling, passing through Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Jingzhou registrar Shao Zai by courier toward Jiangling, passing Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 袁顗馳書報琬，勸勿解甲，並奉勸子勳即偽位。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan sent a swift letter to Wan urging him not to lay down arms and advising Zixun to take the false throne at once.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan wrote in haste urging Wan to keep his armor on and advising Zixun to declare himself emperor immediately.

sentences.zh: 琬乃稱說符瑞，令顧昭之撰為瑞命記。

translations.literal: Wan then proclaimed omens and portents and had Gu Zhaozhi compose a Record of Auspicious Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Wan touted miraculous signs and ordered Gu Zhaozhi to draft a Record of the Auspicious Mandate.

sentences.zh: 造乘輿御服，立宗廟，設壇場，矯作崇憲太后璽令，群僚上偽號於子勳。

translations.literal: They made imperial carriages and robes, established an ancestral temple, set up altars, forged an edict under the seal of Empress Dowager Chongxian, and the officials presented the false title to Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: They built imperial carriages and regalia, founded a temple, raised altars, forged orders in Empress Dowager Chongxian's name, and the officials hailed Zixun as emperor.

sentences.zh: 泰始二年正月七日，即位于尋陽城。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the second year of Taishi he took the throne in Xunyang city.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the first month, Taishi year 2, he was enthroned at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 改景和三年為義嘉元年。

translations.literal: The third year of Jinghe was changed to the first year of Yijia.
translations.idiomatic: The era was changed from Jinghe year 3 to Yijia year 1.

sentences.zh: 其日雲雨晦合，行禮忘稱萬歲。

translations.literal: That day clouds and rain were dark and merged; in performing the rites they forgot to shout "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Clouds and rain closed in that day; during the rites they forgot to cry "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 取子勳所乘車除腳以為輦，置偽殿之西，其夕有鳩棲其中，鴞集其幰，又有禿鶖鳥集城上。

translations.literal: They took the carriage Zixun had ridden, removed its shafts to make an imperial palanquin, and placed it west of the false hall; that evening a dove roosted in it, owls gathered on its canopy, and bald storks perched on the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: They stripped the shafts from Zixun's carriage to make a palanquin and set it west of the false hall. That night a dove nested in it, owls on the canopy, bald storks on the walls.

sentences.zh: 拜安陸王子綏為司徒，因雷電晦冥，震其黃合柱，鴟尾墮地。

translations.literal: When Prince Zisui of Anlu was appointed Minister of State, thunder and lightning darkened the sky and struck the Yellow Registry pillar; the owl-tail ornament fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: As Prince Zisui of Anlu was named Minister of State, thunder darkened the sky, struck the Yellow Registry pillar, and knocked the owl-tail finial to earth.

sentences.zh: 又有鴟棲其帳上。

translations.literal: An owl also perched on his canopy.
translations.idiomatic: An owl roosted on his tent as well.

sentences.zh: 琬性鄙闇，貪吝過甚，財貨酒食，皆身自量校。

translations.literal: Wan by nature was coarse and dull, and excessively greedy and stingy; goods, money, wine, and food he all measured and checked himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was vulgar, dim, and miserly beyond measure—he personally weighed every coin, ration, and cup.

sentences.zh: 至是父子並賣官鬻爵，使婢僕出市道販賣，酣歌博弈，日夜不休。

translations.literal: Now father and son alike sold offices and titles, sent maidservants and servants into the streets to trade, and sang, drank, gambled, and played without cease day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son now sold offices, sent servants to hawk goods in the markets, and drank, sang, and gambled without pause.

sentences.zh: 賓客到門者，曆旬不得前。

translations.literal: Guests who came to the door might wait half a month without being admitted.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors could wait ten days at the gate without seeing them.

sentences.zh: 內事悉委褚靈嗣等三人，群小競為威福，士庶忿怨，內外離心矣。

translations.literal: Internal affairs were entirely entrusted to Chu Lingsi and two others; petty men vied for power and favor, gentry and commoners were full of resentment, and court and country were estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Domestic affairs went to Chu Lingsi and two confederates; lackeys fought for spoils, the people seethed, and the regime lost heart within and without.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣領軍將軍王玄謨領水軍南討，吳興太守張永為繼。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent the Director of the Palace Guard Wang Xuemo to lead the naval forces south in punitive campaign, with the Administrator of Wuxing Zhang Yong as successor force.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Wang Xuemo at the head of the fleet south, with Zhang Yong of Wuxing to follow.

sentences.zh: 尚書下符：「奉詔以四王幼弱，不幸陷難，兵交之日，不得妄加侵犯。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing issued a command: "By imperial decree: the four princes are young and weak and have unfortunately fallen into peril; on the day arms are joined, none may rashly harm them."
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing proclaimed: "By decree—the four princes are young and trapped in disaster; when battle is joined, none may harm them rashly."

sentences.zh: 若有逼損，誅翦無貸。」

translations.literal: "Whoever presses or injures them shall be executed without mercy."
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever harms them will be cut down without pardon."

sentences.zh: 琬遣孫沖之等前鋒一萬據赭圻，沖之於道與子勳書，欲沿流掛帆，直取白下，請速遣陶亮眾軍相接，分據新亭。

translations.literal: Wan sent Sun Chongzhi and others with ten thousand vanguard troops to hold Zheqi; on the road Chongzhi wrote to Zixun proposing to set sail upstream, take Baixia directly, and asking that Tao Liang's army be sent at once to link up and seize Xinting separately.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Sun Chongzhi with ten thousand men to hold Zheqi. Chongzhi wrote urging Zixun to sail upstream straight for Baixia and begged Tao Liang to advance and occupy Xinting.

sentences.zh: 亮本無干略，聞建安王休仁自上，殷孝祖又至，不敢進。

translations.literal: Liang originally had no capacity for command; hearing that Prince Xiuren of Jian'an was coming down from the north and Yin Xiaozu had also arrived, he did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liang lacked military talent. Learning that Prince Xiuren of Jian'an and Yin Xiaozu were approaching, he held back.

sentences.zh: 及孝祖中流矢死，沈攸之代為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Xiaozu was struck by a stray arrow and died, Shen Youzhi replaced him as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozu fell to a stray arrow; Shen Youzhi took the van in his place.

sentences.zh: 沖之謂陶亮曰：「孝祖梟將，一戰便死，天下事定矣，不須復戰。

translations.literal: Chongzhi said to Tao Liang: "Xiaozu was a fierce commander; he died in a single battle—the realm is settled, there is no need to fight again."
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi told Tao Liang, "Xiaozu was a formidable fighter—one battle killed him. The empire is decided; why fight again?"

sentences.zh: 便當直取京都。

translations.literal: We should march straight on the capital at once.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to march on the capital immediately.

sentences.zh: 」亮不從。

translations.literal: Liang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Liang refused.

sentences.zh: 明帝遣員外散騎侍郎王道隆至赭圻督戰，眾軍奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming sent the Supernumerary Palace Attendant Wang Daolong to Zheqi to supervise the battle; the armies struck fiercely and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming sent Wang Daolong to direct the fight at Zheqi; the loyal troops charged and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 琬又遣豫州刺史劉胡來屯鵲尾。

translations.literal: Wan again sent the Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Hu to encamp at Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: Wan sent Liu Hu, Inspector of Yuzhou, to hold Quewei.

sentences.zh: 胡宿將，攸之等甚憚之。

translations.literal: Hu was a veteran commander, and Youzhi and the others greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was a seasoned commander, and Youzhi's side feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 胡鄉人蔡那、佼長生、張敬兒各領軍隸攸之在赭圻，胡因要那等共語。

translations.literal: Hu's fellow townsmen Cai Na, Jiao Changsheng, and Zhang Jing'er each commanded troops under Youzhi at Zheqi; Hu summoned them to speak together.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's countrymen Cai Na, Jiao Changsheng, and Zhang Jing'er served under Youzhi at Zheqi; Hu called them to parley.

sentences.zh: 那等說令歸順。

translations.literal: They persuaded him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: They talked him into surrendering.

sentences.zh: 胡回軍入鵲尾，無他權略。

translations.literal: Hu withdrew his army into Quewei and had no other stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Hu drew back into Quewei with no further plan.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁自武檻進據赭圻，時胡等兵眾強盛，遠近疑惑。

translations.literal: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an advanced from Wujian to hold Zheqi; at the time Hu and the others had strong forces, and near and far were uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiuren marched from Wujian to Zheqi while Hu's army still looked formidable, leaving loyalists uneasy.

sentences.zh: 明帝欲綏慰人情，遣吏部尚書褚彥回至武檻，選用將帥以下。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming wished to soothe hearts and sent the Minister of Personnel Chu Yanhui to Wujian to appoint commanders and officers down the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: To steady morale Ming sent Chu Yanhui of the Ministry of Personnel to Wujian to name officers and commanders.

sentences.zh: 申謙、杜幼文因此求黃門，沈懷明、劉亮求中書郎。

translations.literal: Shen Qian and Du Youwen thereupon sought posts as Palace Attendants; Shen Huaiming and Liu Liang sought posts as Central Secretariat Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qian and Du Youwen asked for Palace Attendant posts; Shen Huaiming and Liu Liang for Secretariat posts.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁即使彥回擬選，上不許，曰：「忠臣殉國，不謀其報，臨難以幹朝典，豈為下之節。」

translations.literal: Prince Xiuren had Yanhui draft the appointments, but the emperor did not consent, saying: "Loyal ministers die for the state without calculating reward; to seek court offices amid peril is not conduct fit for subordinates."
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren had Yanhui draft the list, but the emperor refused: "True servants die for the state without bargaining; to seek promotion in crisis is unworthy of a subject."

sentences.zh: 沈攸之等與劉胡相持久不決，上又遣強弩將軍任農夫等領兵繼至。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and the others were locked with Liu Hu in a prolonged stalemate; the emperor again sent the General of Powerful Crossbows Ren Nongfu and others with reinforcing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi and Hu fought to a standstill until Ming sent Ren Nongfu and more troops.

sentences.zh: 攸之繕修船舸，板材不周，計無所出。

translations.literal: Youzhi was repairing ships but lacked planks and could find no solution.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was rebuilding his fleet but had no timber and no answer.

sentences.zh: 會琬送五千片榜供胡軍用，俄而風潮奔迅，榜突柵出江，胡等力不能制，趁流而下，泊攸之等營，於是材板大足。

translations.literal: It happened that Wan sent five thousand planks for Hu's army; soon wind and tide surged, the planks broke through the palisade into the river, Hu and the others could not control them, and they drifted down to moor at Youzhi's camp—thereafter timber was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Wan dispatched five thousand planks for Hu; a gale drove them through the boom into the river. Hu could not stop them—they drifted to Youzhi's camp, and suddenly he had wood enough.

sentences.zh: 琬進袁顗都督征討諸軍事，率樓船千艘來入鵲尾。

translations.literal: Wan advanced Yuan Yan to overall command of the armies for suppression and led a thousand tower ships into Quewei.
translations.idiomatic: Wan made Yuan Yan supreme commander and led a thousand warships into Quewei.

sentences.zh: 張興世建議越鵲尾上據錢溪，斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi proposed passing above Quewei to seize Qianxi and cut their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi urged bypassing Quewei to hold Qianxi and sever their supplies.

sentences.zh: 胡累攻之不能克，乃遣龍驤將軍陳慶領三百舸向錢溪，戒慶不須戰。

translations.literal: Hu repeatedly attacked but could not overcome him; he then sent the Dragon-Charger General Chen Qing with three hundred boats toward Qianxi, instructing Qing not to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Hu assaulted him in vain, then sent Chen Qing with three hundred boats toward Qianxi, ordering him not to engage.

sentences.zh: 陳慶至錢溪不敢攻，越溪于梅根立砦。

translations.literal: Chen Qing reached Qianxi but did not dare attack, crossed the stream at Meigen, and built a fort.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qing reached Qianxi, refused battle, crossed to Meigen, and threw up a camp.

sentences.zh: 胡別遣將王起領百舸攻興世，擊大破之，胡率其餘舸馳還。

translations.literal: Hu separately sent the general Wang Qi with a hundred boats to attack Xingshi, was struck and utterly defeated, and Hu himself drove the remaining boats back in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent Wang Qi with a hundred boats against Xingshi and was smashed; Hu fled with what was left.

sentences.zh: 顗更使胡攻興世。

translations.literal: Yan again ordered Hu to attack Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan ordered Hu to strike Xingshi again.

sentences.zh: 休仁因此命沈攸之、吳喜、佼長生、劉靈遺、劉伯符等進攻濃湖，造皮艦千乘，拔其營柵，苦戰移日，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiuren therefore ordered Shen Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, Liu Bofu, and others to attack Nonghu, built a thousand leather assault boats, tore out their palisades, fought bitterly all day, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren sent Youzhi, Wu Xi, Jiao Changsheng, Liu Lingyi, and Liu Bofu against Nonghu with a thousand leather assault craft, ripped their stockade, fought all day, and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 顗被攻急，馳信召胡令還。

translations.literal: Yan, pressed hard, sent a swift message summoning Hu back.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Yan recalled Hu by urgent dispatch.

sentences.zh: 張興世既據錢溪，江路阻斷，胡軍乏食。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi having seized Qianxi, the river route was cut and Hu's army lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xingshi held Qianxi the river line was cut and Hu's men starved.

sentences.zh: 琬大送資糧，畏興世不敢下。

translations.literal: Wan sent great quantities of provisions but feared Xingshi and did not dare descend.
translations.idiomatic: Wan shipped vast stores of grain but dared not run past Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 胡遣將迎之，為錢溪所破，夜走徑趣梅根。

translations.literal: Hu sent generals to meet the convoy; they were broken at Qianxi, fled by night, and made straight for Meigen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu sent escorts; Xingshi destroyed them; they fled by night toward Meigen.

sentences.zh: 顗聞胡走，亦棄眾西奔，至青林見殺。

translations.literal: When Yan heard Hu had fled, he too abandoned his troops and fled west; at Qinglin he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Hu had run, Yan abandoned his army and fled west to Qinglin, where he was slain.

sentences.zh: 琬惶擾無計，時張悅始發兄子浩喪，乃稱疾呼琬計事，令左右伏甲戒之，若聞索酒便出。

translations.literal: Wan was frantic and without plan; Zhang Yue had just begun mourning for his elder brother's son Hao and feigned illness to summon Wan for counsel, ordering attendants with armor hidden and instructing them that if wine was requested they should come out.
translations.idiomatic: Wan panicked. Zhang Yue, mourning his nephew Hao, feigned sickness, called Wan to plot, hid armed men, and told them to emerge if he called for wine.

sentences.zh: 琬至，謀斬晉安王，封府庫以謝罪。

translations.literal: When Wan arrived they plotted to kill the Prince of Jin'an, seal the treasury, and plead guilty.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to kill Prince Zixun of Jin'an, seal the treasury, and sue for mercy.

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「寧可賣殿下求活邪。

translations.literal: Yue said: "How could one sell the prince to buy one's life?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Would you sell your prince to save your skin?"

sentences.zh: 」因呼求酒，再呼，左右震懾不能應，第二子詢提刀出，余人續至，即斬琬。

translations.literal: He then called for wine; at the second call his attendants, trembling, did not respond; his second son Xun drew a blade and came out, others followed, and Wan was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: He called for wine; at the second call his men froze; his son Xun drew a sword, others rushed in, and Wan was killed.

sentences.zh: 悅因齎琬首詣建安王休仁降。

translations.literal: Yue then carried Wan's head to Prince Xiuren of Jian'an and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yue took Wan's head to Xiuren and submitted.

sentences.zh: 蔡那子道深以父為明帝效力被系作部，因亂脫鎖入城，執子勳囚之。

translations.literal: Cai Na's son Daoshen, because his father served Ming, had been bound as a prisoner of war; in the chaos he broke his shackles, entered the city, and seized Zixun as a captive.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Na's son Daoshen, whose father fought for Ming, had been chained as a captive; in the turmoil he broke free, entered the city, and seized Zixun.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之諸軍至江州，斬子勳于桑尾牙下，傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's armies reached Jiangzhou, they beheaded Zixun beneath the standard at Sangwei and sent his head to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi's troops reached Jiangzhou, beheaded Zixun under the banner at Sangwei, and sent his head to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 劉胡走入沔，竟陵郡丞陳懷直，憲子也，斷道邀之。

translations.literal: Liu Hu fled into Mian; Chen Huaizhi, assistant magistrate of Jingling and son of Xian, blocked the road to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu fled into Mian; Chen Huaizhi, Jingling assistant and Xian's son, barred the road.

sentences.zh: 胡人馬既疲困，因隨懷直入城，告渴得酒，飲酒畢，引佩刀自刺不死，斬首送建鄴。

translations.literal: Hu's men and horses were already exhausted; he followed Huaizhi into the city, said he was thirsty and was given wine; when he had drunk he drew his belt dagger to stab himself but did not die, and was beheaded and his head sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu and his horses were spent; he entered the city with Huaizhi, begged wine, drank, tried to stab himself with his dagger, failed, and was beheaded—his head sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 張興世弟僧彥追殺懷直，取胡首，竊有其功。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi's younger brother Sengyan pursued and killed Huaizhi, took Hu's head, and stole the credit.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi's brother Sengyan killed Huaizhi, took Hu's head, and claimed the prize wrongly.

sentences.zh: 荊州聞濃湖平，更議奉子頊奔益州就蕭惠開。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou heard Nonghu was pacified, they again discussed supporting Prince Zixu of Linhai to flee to Yizhou and join Xiao Huikai.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou, hearing Nonghu had fallen, debated sending Prince Zixu of Linhai west to Xiao Huikai in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 典簽阮道預、邵宰不同，曰：「雖復欲西，豈可得至。

translations.literal: The registrars Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai disagreed, saying: "Even if you still wish to go west, how could you arrive?"
translations.idiomatic: Registrars Ruan Daoyu and Shao Zai objected: "You may still want the west, but you will never get there."

sentences.zh: 」遣使歸罪。

translations.literal: They sent envoys to confess guilt.
translations.idiomatic: They sent messengers to surrender and plead guilt.

sentences.zh: 荊州中從事宗景、土人姚儉等勒兵入城，執子頊以降。

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat aide Zong Jing and the local leader Yao Jian and others led troops into the city, seized Prince Zixu, and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Jing of the secretariat staff and Yao Jian of the locality led soldiers in, seized Prince Zixu, and yielded.

sentences.zh: 劉胡，南陽涅陽人也，本以面坳黑似胡，故名坳胡，及長單名胡焉。

translations.literal: Liu Hu was a native of Niyang in Nanyang; originally because his face was sunken and black like a barbarian's he was called Ao Hu, and when grown he bore the single name Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu came from Niyang in Nanyang. His sunken, dark face earned him the nickname Ao Hu; in adulthood he was known simply as Hu.

sentences.zh: 出身郡將，稍至隊主。

translations.literal: He began as a commandery officer and gradually rose to platoon chief.
translations.idiomatic: He started as a commandery soldier and rose to platoon chief.

sentences.zh: 討伐諸蠻，往無不捷。

translations.literal: In campaigns against the various Man he was never unsuccessful.
translations.idiomatic: Against the Man tribes he never lost.

sentences.zh: 蠻甚畏憚之。

translations.literal: The Man greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: The Man dreaded him.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，除越騎校尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he was made Commandant of Elite Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming's accession he became Commandant of Elite Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 蠻畏之，小兒啼，語云：「劉胡來。

translations.literal: The Man feared him; when small children cried, people would say: "Liu Hu is coming."
translations.idiomatic: The Man feared him so much that mothers hushed crying children with "Liu Hu is coming!"

sentences.zh: 」便止。

translations.literal: They then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The children fell silent.

sentences.zh: 宗越，南陽葉人也。

translations.literal: Zong Yue was a native of Ye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yue came from Ye in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 本為南陽次門。

translations.literal: He was originally registered as a secondary household of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His household had been classed as a secondary Nanyang clan.

sentences.zh: 安北將軍趙倫之鎮襄陽，襄陽多雜姓，越更被黜為役門。

translations.literal: When the General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Lunzhi held Xiangyang, Xiangyang had many mixed surnames, and Yue was further demoted to a corvée household.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Lunzhi pacified the north from Xiangyang—a city of many mixed clans—Yue was demoted again to corvée status.

sentences.zh: 出身補郡吏。

translations.literal: He entered service as a supplement to the commandery clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a supplemental commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 父為蠻所殺，越於市中刺殺讎人。

translations.literal: His father was killed by the Man; Yue stabbed the killer to death in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The Man killed his father; Yue ran the killer through in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 太守夏侯穆嘉其意，擢為隊主。

translations.literal: The Administrator Xia Hou Mu admired his spirit and promoted him to platoon chief.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Xia Hou Mu honored his resolve and made him platoon chief.

sentences.zh: 蠻有為寇盜者，常使越討伐，往輒有功。

translations.literal: Whenever the Man raided, he was often sent to suppress them and always had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Man plundered, they sent Yue; he always won.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以市馬，刀楯步出，單身挺戰，眾莫能當。

translations.literal: His family was poor and could not buy a horse; he went out on foot with blade and shield, fought alone in the press, and none could withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor for a horse, he marched with blade and shield, fought alone in the melee, and none could stand against him.

sentences.zh: 每一捷，郡將輒賞錢五千，因此得買馬。

translations.literal: After each victory the commandery officer would reward him five thousand cash, and thus he was able to buy a horse.
translations.idiomatic: Each victory brought five thousand cash from the commandery officer, and at last he bought a horse.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十四年，啟文帝求復次門，移戶屬冠軍縣，許之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia he petitioned Emperor Wen to restore his household to secondary status and transfer his registration to Guanjun county; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 24 he asked Emperor Wen to restore his secondary-household standing and move his register to Guanjun; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，隨柳元景侵魏，領馬幢隸柳元怙有戰功，還補後軍參軍督護，隨王誕戲之曰：「汝何人，遂得我府四字。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he followed Liu Yuanjing in the invasion of Wei, led the horse pennant under Liu Yuanku with battle merit, and on return was made Rear Army Staff Officer and Protector; Prince Dan of Sui jested with him: "What sort of man are you, to win a four-character title in my headquarters?"
translations.idiomatic: In year 27 he joined Liu Yuanjing's Wei campaign, led horse pennants under Liu Yuanku with distinction, and returned as Rear Army staff officer and protector. Prince Dan of Sui teased him: "Who are you to earn a four-character post in my command?"

sentences.zh: 」越答曰：「佛狸未死，不憂不得諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Yue answered: "Buddha Li is not yet dead—I need not worry about becoming a Consultation Staff Officer."
translations.idiomatic: Yue replied, "Buddha Li still lives—I'll yet be a consultation staff officer."

sentences.zh: 」誕大笑。

translations.literal: Dan laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Dan roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，為長水校尉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming he was made Commandant of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year 3 he became Commandant of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王誕據廣陵反，越領馬軍隸沈慶之攻誕。

translations.literal: When Prince Dan of Jingling held Guangling in rebellion, Yue led the horse troops under Shen Qingzhi to attack Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Dan of Jingling rebelled at Guangling, Yue led cavalry under Shen Qingzhi against him.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，孝武使悉殺城內男丁。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Emperor Xiaowu ordered all males within the walls to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Emperor Xiaowu ordered every male in it put to death.

sentences.zh: 越受旨行誅，躬臨其事，莫不先加捶撻，或有鞭其面者，欣欣然若有所得，凡殺數千人。

translations.literal: Yue received the order to carry out the executions and personally oversaw the matter; none escaped a beating first, and some were flogged in the face; he was gleeful as though he had gained something, and in all he killed several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to execute the slaughter, Yue supervised it himself. Every victim was beaten first—some flogged in the face—and he looked pleased, as if at a prize. He killed several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 改封始安縣子。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Viscount of Shi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Viscount of Shi'an.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝景和元年，進爵為侯，召為遊擊將軍、直合，領南濟陰太守，改領南東海太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe under the deposed emperor he was advanced to marquis, summoned as General of Mobile Strikes and Palace Guard, made concurrent Administrator of Southern Jiyin, then transferred to Administrator of Southern Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe year 1 under the deposed emperor he rose to marquis, became General of Mobile Strikes and a palace guard officer, held Southern Jiyin, then Southern Donghai.

sentences.zh: 帝凶暴無道，而越、譚金、童太一併為之用命，誅戮群公及何邁等，莫不盡心竭力，故帝憑其爪牙，無所忌憚。

translations.literal: The emperor was ferocious and lawless, yet Yue, Tan Jin, and Tong Taiyi all obeyed his orders; in executing the great ministers and He Mai and the rest they spared no effort, so the emperor relied on these claws and fangs without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was savage and cruel, but Yue, Tan Jin, and Tong Taiyi did his bidding. They hunted down ministers and He Mai with brutal zeal, and he leaned on them without fear.

sentences.zh: 賜與越等美女金帛，充牣其家。

translations.literal: He bestowed on Yue and the others beautiful women and gold and silk, filling their houses to overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: He showered them with women, gold, and silk until their houses overflowed.

sentences.zh: 越等武人粗強，識不及遠，感一往意氣，皆無復二心。

translations.literal: Yue and the others were rough warriors of limited vision; stirred by a burst of loyalty, none harbored a second thought.
translations.idiomatic: These rough soldiers could not see far; a flash of personal loyalty left them without second thoughts.

sentences.zh: 帝時南巡，明旦便發，其夕悉聽越等出外宿，明帝因此定亂。

translations.literal: When the emperor was on southern tour and would set out at dawn the next day, that evening he allowed Yue and the others to lodge outside; Emperor Ming thereby settled the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured south and meant to leave at dawn. That night he let Yue and the rest sleep outside the palace—giving Ming his chance to seize power.

sentences.zh: 明晨越等併入，被撫接甚厚。

translations.literal: The next morning Yue and the others all entered together and were received with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Next morning they entered court and were treated with elaborate courtesy.

sentences.zh: 越改領南濟陰太守，本官如故。

translations.literal: Yue was transferred to Administrator of Southern Jiyin; his original posts remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was shifted to Southern Jiyin while keeping his other titles.

sentences.zh: 越等既為廢帝盡心，慮明帝不能容之。

translations.literal: Yue and the others, having served the deposed emperor with all their hearts, feared Emperor Ming could not tolerate them.
translations.idiomatic: Having served the deposed emperor faithfully, they feared Ming would not spare them.

sentences.zh: 上接待雖厚，內並懷懼。

translations.literal: Though the emperor received them generously, inwardly they were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The throne welcomed them warmly, yet each man was afraid within.

sentences.zh: 上意亦不欲使其居中，從容謂曰：「卿遭離暴朝，勤勞日久，兵馬大郡，隨卿等所擇。

translations.literal: The emperor also did not wish them at the center and said gently: "You endured a violent court and labored long; choose any great commandery of horse and arms as you please."
translations.idiomatic: Ming did not want them at court and said gently, "You suffered under a tyrant and served long. Choose any great military commandery you wish."

sentences.zh: 」越等素已自疑，及聞此旨，皆相顧失色。

translations.literal: Yue and the others had already been suspicious; on hearing this intent they looked at one another and turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Already uneasy, they exchanged glances and went white at the words.

sentences.zh: 因謀作難，以告沈攸之，攸之具白帝，即日下獄死。

translations.literal: They therefore plotted trouble and told Shen Youzhi; Youzhi reported fully to the emperor, and that same day they were imprisoned and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted revolt and confided in Shen Youzhi, who told the emperor everything. That day they were jailed and executed.

sentences.zh: 越善立營陣，每數萬人止頓，自騎馬前行，使軍人隨其後，馬止營合，未嘗參差。

translations.literal: Yue was skilled at setting camp formations; when tens of thousands halted, he rode ahead on horseback and had the soldiers follow; when his horse stopped the camp closed up without ever falling out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Yue excelled at encampments. With tens of thousands on the march he rode ahead; when he halted, the camp formed without a gap.

sentences.zh: 及沈攸之代殷孝祖為南討前鋒，時孝祖新死，眾心並懼。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi replaced Yin Xiaozu as vanguard of the southern campaign, Xiaozu had just died and every heart was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi replaced the fallen Yin Xiaozu as southern vanguard, the army was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 攸之歎曰：「宗公可惜，故有勝人處。

translations.literal: Youzhi sighed and said: "Lord Zong was a loss—he had his superior points."
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi sighed, "A pity about Lord Zong—he had his strengths."

sentences.zh: 」而性嚴酷，好行刑誅，時王玄謨禦下亦少恩，將士為之語曰：「寧作五年徒，不逐王玄謨，玄謨猶尚可，宗越更殺我。」

translations.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and he loved punishments and executions; at the time Wang Xuemo too showed little kindness to subordinates, and the soldiers had a saying: "Better five years as a convict than follow Wang Xuemo; Xuemo is still tolerable, but Zong Yue will kill me."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was cruel and fond of killing. Soldiers said, "Better five years as a convict than serve Wang Xuemo—Xuemo is bearable, but Zong Yue will kill you."

sentences.zh: 譚金在魏時，與薛安都有舊，後出新野居牛門村。

translations.literal: Tan Jin in Wei times had been on familiar terms with Xue Andou; later he came out to Xinye and lived at Niumen village.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei service Tan Jin had known Xue Andou; later he settled at Niumen in Xinye.

sentences.zh: 及安都歸國，金常隨征討，副安都，排堅陷陣，氣力兼人。

translations.literal: When Andou returned to the Song, Jin often followed on campaigns as his deputy, breaking strong points and charging formations, with strength surpassing ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: When Andou defected south, Jin campaigned at his side as deputy, breaching lines with superhuman force.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，為屯騎校尉、直合，領南清河太守。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian he was Commandant of the Escort Cavalry and Palace Guard, concurrent Administrator of Southern Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year 3 he was Commandant of Escort Cavalry, palace guard, and Administrator of Southern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 景和元年，前廢帝誅群公，金等並為之用，封金平都縣男，童太一宜陽縣男，沈攸之東興縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jinghe the deposed emperor executed the great ministers; Jin and the others all served him; Jin was enfeoffed Baron of Pingdu, Tong Taiyi Baron of Yiyang, and Shen Youzhi Baron of Dongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinghe year 1 the deposed emperor slaughtered the ministers. Jin was made Baron of Pingdu, Tong Taiyi of Yiyang, Youzhi of Dongxing.

sentences.zh: 越州裏又有武念、佼長生、曹欣之、蔡那並以將帥顯。

translations.literal: In Yuezhou district there were also Wu Nian, Jiao Changsheng, Cao Xinzhi, and Cai Na, all distinguished as commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Around Yue district Wu Nian, Jiao Changsheng, Cao Xinzhi, and Cai Na also rose as noted commanders.

sentences.zh: 武念位至南陽太守，長生甯蠻校尉，曹欣之驍騎將軍；

translations.literal: Wu Nian rose to Administrator of Nanyang, Changsheng to Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, and Cao Xinzhi to General of Valiant Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Nian became Administrator of Nanyang, Changsheng Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, Cao Xinzhi General of Valiant Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 蔡那見子道恭傳。

translations.literal: Cai Na is treated in the biography of his son Daogong.
translations.idiomatic: on Cai Na see the biography of his son Daogong.

sentences.zh: 吳喜，吳興臨安人也。

translations.literal: Wu Xi was a native of Lin'an in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi came from Lin'an in Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 本名喜公，明帝減為喜。

translations.literal: His original name was Xigong; Emperor Ming shortened it to Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Born Xigong, he was renamed Xi when Emperor Ming shortened the name.

sentences.zh: 出身為領軍府白衣吏。

translations.literal: He began as a white-robed clerk in the Director of the Palace Guard's office.
translations.idiomatic: He started as an unpaid clerk in the palace guard directorate.

sentences.zh: 少知書，領軍將軍沈演之使寫起居注，所寫既畢，闇誦略皆上口。

translations.literal: From youth he knew writing; the Director Shen Yanzhi had him copy the imperial diary, and when the copying was done he could recite it from memory almost entirely by heart.
translations.idiomatic: He could read from youth. Shen Yanzhi had him copy the imperial diary; when finished he could recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 演之嘗作讓表，未奏失本，喜經一見即寫，無所漏脫。

translations.literal: Yanzhi once drafted a memorial of resignation that had not yet been submitted when the draft was lost; Xi had seen it once and wrote it out with nothing omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi lost a draft resignation memorial before it was filed; Xi had seen it once and reproduced it without omission.

sentences.zh: 演之甚知之。

translations.literal: Yanzhi thought very highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi prized him highly.

sentences.zh: 因此涉獵史、漢，頗見古今。

translations.literal: Thereby he browsed the histories and gained considerable knowledge of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: He then read histories and gained a working knowledge of past and present.

sentences.zh: 演之門生朱重人入為主書，薦喜為主書吏，進為主圖令史。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's student Zhu Chongren entered service as Master of Documents and recommended Xi as a documents clerk; he advanced to Master of Maps clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Student Zhu Chongren became Master of Documents, recommended Xi as clerk, and promoted him to maps archivist.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗求圖書，喜開卷倒進之，帝怒遣出。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once asked for books; Xi opened the scroll and presented it upside down; the emperor in anger sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen requested a book; Xi handed it in upside down and was dismissed in anger.

sentences.zh: 會太子步兵校尉沈慶之征蠻，啟文帝請喜自隨，為孝武所知。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince's Commandant of Footsoldiers Shen Qingzhi campaigned against the Man, he petitioned Emperor Wen to take Xi with him, and Xi came to Xiaowu's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi campaigning against the Man asked Wen to let Xi accompany him, and Xiaowu took notice of Xi.

sentences.zh: 稍遷至河東太守、殿中御史。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Administrator of Hedong and Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Hedong and palace censor.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，四方反叛，喜請得精兵三百致死於東。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne and rebellion broke out on all sides, Xi asked for three hundred elite troops to die fighting in the east.
translations.idiomatic: At Ming's accession, with revolt everywhere, Xi asked for three hundred picked men to die fighting in the east.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，即假建武將軍，簡羽林勇士配之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and at once made him acting General Who Establishes Martial Might, selecting Palace Guard champions to assign him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, named him acting General Who Establishes Martial Might, and gave him picked guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 議者以喜刀筆吏，不嚐為將，不可遣。

translations.literal: Critics said Xi was a clerk and had never been a general and could not be sent.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said a clerk who had never commanded troops should not be sent.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人巢尚之曰：「喜隨沈慶之累經軍旅，性既勇決，又習戰陣，若能任之，必有成績。

translations.literal: The Secretariat Gentleman Chao Shangzhi said: "Xi followed Shen Qingzhi through many campaigns; his nature is bold and resolute and he is practiced in battle; if you entrust him, he will certainly achieve results."
translations.idiomatic: Chao Shangzhi of the Secretariat said, "Xi followed Qingzhi through many wars—bold, resolute, trained in battle. Entrust him and he will deliver."

sentences.zh: 」喜乃東討。

translations.literal: Xi then campaigned east.
translations.idiomatic: Xi marched east.

sentences.zh: 喜在孝武世既見驅使，性寬厚，所至人並懷之。

translations.literal: Xi in Xiaowu's time had already been employed; his nature was generous, and wherever he went people were drawn to him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaowu Xi had already been used; generous by nature, he won people wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 及東討，百姓聞吳河東來，便望風降散，故喜所至克捷。

translations.literal: On the eastern campaign, when the people heard that Wu of Hedong was coming, they surrendered at the rumor and scattered, so wherever Xi went he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern campaign the people heard "Wu of Hedong is coming" and surrendered in waves, so Xi won with ease.

sentences.zh: 遷步兵校尉，封竟陵縣侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commandant of Footsoldiers and enfeoffed Marquis of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: He became Commandant of Footsoldiers and Marquis of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 東土平定，又率所領南討，遷尋陽太守。

translations.literal: When the east was pacified he again led his command south in punitive campaign and was made Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the east was pacified he led troops south again and was made Administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年，改封東興縣侯，除右軍將軍、淮陽太守，兼太子左衛率。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taishi his fief was changed to Marquis of Dongxing; he was made General of the Right Army, Administrator of Huaiyang, and concurrent Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year 4 he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongxing, General of the Right Army, Administrator of Huaiyang, and Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉驍騎將軍，太守、兼率如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry; his posts as administrator and commandant remained.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he became General of Valiant Cavalry while keeping his other posts.

sentences.zh: 其年，大破魏軍于荊亭。

translations.literal: That year he inflicted a great defeat on Wei forces at Jingting.
translations.idiomatic: That year he crushed Wei armies at Jingting.

sentences.zh: 六年，又率軍向豫州拒魏軍，加都督豫州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again led an army toward Yuzhou to resist Wei and was given overall command of Yuzhou military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he marched to Yuzhou against Wei with overall command of its armies.

sentences.zh: 明年還建鄴。

translations.literal: The following year he returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 初，喜東征，白明帝得尋陽王子房及諸賊帥即於東梟斬。

translations.literal: At first, when Xi campaigned east, he told Emperor Ming that on capturing Prince Zifang of Xunyang and the other rebel leaders he would behead them in the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi first marched east he promised Ming he would behead Prince Zifang of Xunyang and the rebel chiefs on the spot.

sentences.zh: 東土既平，喜見南賊方熾，慮後翻覆受禍，乃生送子房還都。

translations.literal: After the east was pacified, Xi saw southern rebels still strong and feared later reversal and punishment; he therefore sent Zifang alive back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the east was quiet he feared southern rebels might later ruin him, so he sent Zifang alive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 凡諸大主帥顧琛、王曇生之徒皆被全活。

translations.literal: All the great commanders such as Gu Chen and Wang Tansheng were likewise spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: Great commanders like Gu Chen and Wang Tansheng were also spared.

sentences.zh: 上以喜新立大功，不問而心銜之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xi had just won a great victory, did not question him but bore a grudge in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ming did not punish Xi for his fresh triumph but nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 及平荊州，恣意剽虜，贓私萬計。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was pacified he plundered at will; private gains numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Jingzhou he looted freely, amassing private wealth beyond count.

sentences.zh: 又嘗對客言漢高、魏武本是何人。

translations.literal: He also once said to guests that Gaozu of Han and Emperor Wu of Wei were originally what sort of men.
translations.idiomatic: He once told guests what sort of men Han Gaozu and Wei Wudi had been.

sentences.zh: 上聞之益不悅。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he was still more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew still more displeased.

sentences.zh: 後壽寂之死，喜內懼，因乞中散大夫。

translations.literal: After Shouji's death Xi was inwardly afraid and therefore begged for the post of Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouji's death Xi grew afraid and asked to become a palace cadet.

sentences.zh: 上尤疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected him still more.

sentences.zh: 及上有疾，為身後之慮，疑其將來不能事幼主，乃賜死。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill he made plans for what would follow, doubting that Xi could later serve a young sovereign, and therefore granted him death.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill he doubted Xi would serve a child emperor and ordered him to die.

sentences.zh: 上召入內殿，與言謔酬接甚款，賜以名饌並金銀禦器。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him into the inner hall, spoke and jested with him very cordially, and bestowed famous delicacies and imperial gold and silver vessels.
