translations.idiomatic: He summoned Xi to the inner hall, chatted familiarly, and gave him delicacies and imperial gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 敕將命者勿使食器宿喜家。

translations.literal: He instructed the envoy carrying the order not to let the vessels remain overnight in Xi's house.
translations.idiomatic: He told the executioner not to leave the imperial vessels overnight in Xi's house.

sentences.zh: 上素多忌諱，不欲令食器停凶禍之室故也。

translations.literal: The emperor had many taboos and did not wish vessels to remain in a house of ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Ming was full of taboos and would not let feast ware stay where doom had fallen.

sentences.zh: 及喜死，發詔賻贈，子徽人襲。

translations.literal: When Xi died an edict was issued for funeral gifts; his son Hui inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi died an edict ordered funeral gifts; his son Hui inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 黃回，竟陵郡軍人也。

translations.literal: Huang Hui was a soldier of Jingling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui was a soldier from Jingling commandery.

sentences.zh: 出身充郡府雜使，稍至傳教。

translations.literal: He began as a miscellaneous attendant in the commandery office and gradually rose to transmission instructor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a miscellaneous attendant in the commandery yamen and rose to transmission instructor.

sentences.zh: 臧質為郡，轉為齋帥。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi was in the commandery, Hui was made quartermaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi governed the commandery, Hui became quartermaster.

sentences.zh: 及去職，以回自隨。

translations.literal: When Zhi left office, Hui went with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi left office Hui followed him.

sentences.zh: 質討元凶，回隨從有功，免軍戶。

translations.literal: When Zhi campaigned against the crown prince's crime, Hui followed and had merit, and was released from military household status.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi marched against the usurper Hui followed with merit and was freed from military-household status.

sentences.zh: 後隨質於梁山敗走，被錄，遇赦，因下都。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zhi in defeat and flight at Liangshan, was captured, met amnesty, and thus went down to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later he fled with Zhi from defeat at Liangshan, was captured, amnestied, and went to the capital.

sentences.zh: 于宣陽門與人相打，詐稱江夏王義恭馬客，被鞭二百，付右尚方。

translations.literal: At Xuanyang Gate he fought with someone, falsely claiming to be a client of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, and was flogged two hundred strokes and sent to the Right Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuanyang Gate he brawled, claimed to be a client of Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, was flogged two hundred times, and sent to the Right Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 會中書舍人戴明寶被系，差回為戶伯。

translations.literal: When Secretariat Gentleman Dai Mingbao was imprisoned, Hui was assigned as barracks chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Dai Mingbao of the Secretariat was imprisoned, Hui was made barracks chief over him.

sentences.zh: 奉事明寶，竭心盡力，明寶尋得原赦，委任如初，啟免回以領隨身隊統，知宅及江西墅事。

translations.literal: Serving Mingbao he gave his utmost; Mingbao soon received pardon and entrusted him as before, petitioning to free Hui and make him commander of his personal guard, in charge of the residence and the Jiangxi estate.
translations.idiomatic: He served Mingbao devotedly; Mingbao was pardoned, trusted him again, freed him, and made him head of his personal guard and manager of house and estate.

sentences.zh: 性巧，觸類多能，明寶甚寵任之。

translations.literal: He was clever and capable in many crafts; Mingbao favored and relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Clever at many crafts, he won Mingbao's deep trust.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，桂陽王休範為逆，回以屯騎校尉領軍隸齊高帝，於新亭創詐降之計，回見休範可乘，謂張敬兒曰：「卿可取之，我誓不殺諸王。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyuan, Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled; Hui as Commandant of Escort Cavalry led troops under the Qi emperor at Xinting and devised the false surrender; seeing Xiufan could be taken, he said to Zhang Jing'er: "You can seize him—I swear not to kill princes."
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanyuan's start Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled. Hui, Commandant of Escort Cavalry under the future Qi emperor at Xinting, devised a false surrender and told Zhang Jing'er, "Take him—I swear not to kill princes."

sentences.zh: 」敬兒即日斬休範。

translations.literal: Jing'er that same day beheaded Xiufan.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er beheaded Xiufan the same day.

sentences.zh: 事平，進爵為侯，改封聞喜縣。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled his rank was advanced to marquis and his fief changed to Wenxi county.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he was advanced to marquis and re-enfeoffed in Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷冠軍將軍、南琅邪濟陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made General Who Conquers the Champions and Administrator of the two commanderies of Nanlangye and Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he became General Who Conquers the Champions and Administrator of Nanlangye and Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 建平王景素反，回又率軍前討。

translations.literal: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled, Hui again led troops forward in punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jingsu of Jianping rebelled, Hui led troops against him.

sentences.zh: 城平之日，回軍先入。

translations.literal: On the day the city fell, Hui's army entered first.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Hui's men entered first.

sentences.zh: 又以景素讓張倪奴。

translations.literal: He also yielded Jingsu to Zhang Ninu.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded capture of Jingsu to Zhang Ninu.

sentences.zh: 明年遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: The following year he was made General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之反，以回為平西將軍、郢州刺史，率眾出新亭為前鋒，未發而袁粲據於石頭，不從齊高帝。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Hui was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, leading troops from Xinting as vanguard; before he set out Yuan Can held Shitou and would not follow the Qi emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi rebelled, Hui was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yingzhou, to lead the vanguard from Xinting; before he marched Yuan Can held Shitou against the Qi emperor.

sentences.zh: 回與新亭諸將任候伯、彭文之、王宜興等謀應粲，攻高帝於朝堂。

translations.literal: Hui with the Xinting generals Ren Houbo, Peng Wenzhi, Wang Yixing, and others plotted to answer Can and attack the Qi emperor in the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hui with Ren Houbo, Peng Wenzhi, Wang Yixing, and other Xinting officers plotted with Can to strike the Qi emperor in court.

sentences.zh: 事既不果，高帝撫之如舊。

translations.literal: When the affair failed, the Qi emperor treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The plot failed; the Qi emperor treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 回與宜興素不協，斬之。

translations.literal: Hui and Yixing had long been at odds and he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and Yixing were enemies; he beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 宜興，吳興人也，形狀短小而果勁有膽力，少年時為劫不須伴，郡縣討逐，圍繞數十重，終莫能擒。

translations.literal: Yixing was a man of Wuxing, short in stature but resolute and bold; in youth he robbed alone without companions, and when commanderies and counties pursued and surrounded him in dozens of rings they could never seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Yixing of Wuxing was short but fierce. As a youth he robbed alone; even when surrounded by dozens of pursuers he escaped.

sentences.zh: 嘗舞刀楯，回使十餘人以水交灑不能著。

translations.literal: Once wielding blade and shield, Hui had more than ten men splash water at him crosswise but could not touch him.
translations.idiomatic: Once with blade and shield, a dozen men splashing water at him could not wet him.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始中為將，在壽陽間與魏戰，每以少制多，挺身深入。

translations.literal: In Taishi of Emperor Ming he was a general; between campaigns at Shouyang against Wei he always used few to overcome many and plunged in bodily.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming in the Taishi era he fought at Shouyang against Wei, often beating larger forces by plunging in himself.

sentences.zh: 以平建平王景素功，封長壽縣男。

translations.literal: For pacifying Prince Jingsu of Jianping he was enfeoffed Baron of Changshou.
translations.idiomatic: For suppressing Prince Jingsu he was enfeoffed Baron of Changshou.

sentences.zh: 至是為屯騎校尉，見殺。

translations.literal: At this time he was Commandant of Escort Cavalry and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Commandant of Escort Cavalry, he was killed.

sentences.zh: 回進軍未至郢州而沈攸之敗走。

translations.literal: Hui had advanced but not yet reached Yingzhou when Shen Youzhi was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had not reached Yingzhou when Youzhi was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 回不樂停郢州，固求南兗，遂率部曲輒還，改封安陸郡公，徙南兗州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Hui did not wish to remain at Yingzhou and firmly requested Southern Yanzhou; he then led his personal troops back on his own authority, was changed to Duke of Anlu, and transferred to Inspector of Southern Yanzhou with overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to stay in Yingzhou, he demanded Southern Yanzhou, marched his troops back without leave, was made Duke of Anlu, and became Inspector of Southern Yanzhou with overall command.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝以回專殺，終不附己，乃使召之。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor, because Hui had killed on his own authority and would never attach himself, sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor, seeing Hui's arbitrary killings and refusal to submit, summoned him.

sentences.zh: 及上車，愛妾見赤光冠其頭至足，苦止不肯住。

translations.literal: When he boarded the carriage his beloved concubine saw red light covering him from head to foot and bitterly urged him to stop, but he would not.
translations.idiomatic: As he boarded his carriage his concubine saw red light from head to foot and begged him to stay; he would not.

sentences.zh: 及至見誅。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed on arrival.

sentences.zh: 回既貴，祗事戴明寶甚謹。

translations.literal: Once Hui was eminent he served Dai Mingbao with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated, Hui served Dai Mingbao with scrupulous reverence.

sentences.zh: 言必自名，未嘗敢坐，躬至帳下及入內料檢有無，隨乏供送，以此為常。

translations.literal: In speech he always named himself and never dared sit; he personally went to the tent and entered the inner quarters to check supplies, sending whatever was lacking—this was his constant practice.
translations.idiomatic: He always named himself in speech, never sat in Mingbao's presence, inspected stores in person, and supplied whatever was missing—his daily habit.

sentences.zh: 回同時為將有南郡高道慶，凶險暴橫，求欲無已，有失其意者，輒加捶拉，往往有死者。

translations.literal: Among commanders of Hui's time there was Gao Daoqing of Nan Commandery, violent and overbearing, whose desires knew no limit; those who failed his will he beat, and often men died.
translations.idiomatic: A contemporary commander was Gao Daoqing of Nan Commandery—brutal, insatiable, beating men to death when crossed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷畏之如虎狼。

translations.literal: The court feared him as it would tigers and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared him like a tiger or wolf.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝與袁粲等議，收付廷尉賜死。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor discussed with Yuan Can and others, had him arrested and handed to the Minister of Justice, and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor consulted Yuan Can and the rest, had him seized, handed to the Minister of Justice, and ordered death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：凶人之濟其身業，非世亂其莫由焉。

translations.literal: The commentary says: For violent men to advance their careers, without a chaotic age there would be no means for it.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Violent men could advance their careers only because the age itself was violent—without turmoil they would have had no path.

sentences.zh: 魯爽以亂世之請而行之於平日，其取敗也宜哉。

translations.literal: Liu Shuang applied the license of a chaotic age in times of peace; that he met defeat was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shuang acted in peacetime as if the realm were still in chaos; it is no wonder he was ruined.

sentences.zh: 安都自致奔亡，亦為幸矣。

translations.literal: Andou brought exile on himself by his own doing—this too was a kind of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Andou brought exile on himself—given the alternatives, even that was a kind of mercy.

sentences.zh: 鄧琬以亂濟亂，終致顛隕。

translations.literal: Deng Wan used disorder to aid disorder and in the end met ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan fed rebellion with rebellion and in the end was overthrown.

sentences.zh: 宗越釁稔惡盈，旋至夷戮，各其職也。

translations.literal: Zong Yue's offenses accumulated and his evil filled out; he was soon exterminated—each received his due.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yue's crimes piled up until his wickedness overflowed; swift extermination followed—each man received his due.

sentences.zh: 吳喜以定亂之功，勞未酬而禍集；

translations.literal: Wu Xi for his merit in settling disorder had his reward not yet paid when calamity gathered upon him;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xi, who had pacified rebellion, was destroyed before his service could be rewarded;

sentences.zh: 黃回以助順之志，福未驗而災生，唯命也哉。

translations.literal: Huang Hui for his will to aid the legitimate cause had fortune not yet verified when disaster arose—this was fate alone.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, who had aided the legitimate cause, met disaster before fortune could prove itself—such is fate.
